cues.text: So you were both given your project assignments for your senior thesis today right?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Yes, and we already have to submit our topics next week!
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: But how could they give us a grade this soon?
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: No, next week’s due date will not be counted towards your final grade.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: The teachers are just going to read your topic and give you feedback.
Oh, I see. So first we should come up with our topics, and then what?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Well, once you know what you want to study, you need to think about how you’ll study it.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: You need to decide on your research methods. The methods will be the main part of your paper.
What about the results section?
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: Well, I can give you feedback on that, but you will be the one carrying out an experiment and thus will have to produce the results on your own.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: What I would like to do today is practise writing research papers before you even begin your reports.
I’ll give you samples of old data from past experience, and you can practice writing results and drawing conclusions.
I think that would be really helpful.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Yeah, it sounds like a lot of extra work, but I’m sure it will make our actual project easier.
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: You exactly right. So let’s get started. First, let’s try this simple experiment on fruit flies.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Read the information, and then take 25 minutes to summarise a results and conclusion section. That’s really important - pay attention to the time limit.
OK, does it still have to be 6,000 words?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: No, don’t worry about that
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: What if we get off topic?
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: I wouldn’t worry too much - you will have so much information to write about that it should be easy to stay on topic.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: But what about other sources?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Well for this assignment, you can use the one from your textbook.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: In your actual paper, you should find old experiments that support your topic.
So do we need to find different types of sources? For instance, should I be conducting lots of interviews to use in my paper?
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: No, there’s no need to conduct lots of interviews or anything like that.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: OK, I’m ready to get started. I’m still a little confused though, on how we should format our paper.
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: Don’t worry about it for now, but on your final paper, make sure to pay attention to the format. It should follow the guidelines exactly.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Oh man, I’m starting to understand why they give us all semester to do this.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Are there any other small details like that that we should know about?
Not a whole lot, make sure you provide two copies - one for your teacher of course, but one for yourself as well.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: And of course, you know the due date, right?
Uh, it’s April 11, right?
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: What? No! It’s May 11. Right?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Yes. The due date is May 11. Write it down!
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Oh wow. Yeah, I need to note it. Also, I’m having trouble finding information on my topic. What if i can’t find enough good sources?
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: It’s alright to change your topic. Just make sure to do it before the beginning of April.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Oh really? Wow, I’m definitely going to change it then.
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: Just make sure to write a note to your teacher letting him or her know.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Okay. So getting back to writing this sample paper, where do we start? Should I just explain the experiment and what happened?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Well, you need to start with your hypothesis - what you think will happen - and then describe your procedure.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Then you can write up the results and your conclusions.
Oh boy, I don’t know if I can handle any more instructions…
cues.speaker: Jane
